newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Caltex Indonesia to boost investment, oil output.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Indonesia to boost investment, oil output.

text.p: Indonesia's top foreign oil contractor, PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia, on Friday unveiled plans to boost investment spending and oil output this year.
"We will boost investment to $400 million in 1997 from $344 million in 1996, mainly for exploration and exploitation," Caltex President Baihaki Hakim told Reuters in an interview.

He said Caltex would raise crude oil production to around 785,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1997 from 758,000 bpd in 1996, adding that the Minas and Duri fields in central Sumatra continued to be the backbone of the company's production.
Hakim said the Minas field currently produced 225,000 bpd while Duri's output was 275,000 bpd.

He said Caltex, a 50-50 venture between Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, had received a financial incentive from Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina to further develop the Minas field through a steamflooding project.
Steamflooding is a process in which steam is injected into oil fields to increase production.

"Pertamina has agreed to our proposal for a financial incentive to develop the Minas light oil steamflooding project to recover around 300 million to 400 million barrels of Minas crude oil reserves," he said.
He said the project was very risky and needed investment totalling some $630 million.

"The incentive is in the form of interest recovery for the Minas light oil steamflooding project. This is a case-by-case incentive where we are allowed to charge the interest on our loans as an operating cost," he said.
He said under the current rule Caltex could not charge to Pertamina the interest on loans.
"This Minas project is the first where steamflooding is applied on light crude reserves. We will see the results of the project in 1999," he said.
He said the method was used by Caltex in the Duri field, which contains heavy crude oil.
Hakim said output from the aging Duri field had fallen to 275,000 bpd currently from 300,000 bpd, adding that some 60,000 bpd of Duri crude was used in steamflood injection in the field.
He said Caltex would in the future use natural gas from South Sumatra to replace the Duri crude used in steamflooding.

Indonesia's state-run distributor PT Perusahaan Gas Negara is planning to build a pipeline between a gas field in South Sumatra operated by Asamera Oil Ltd, a unit of Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, and the Duri field.
Hakim said Caltex was still studying the possibility of developing the Duri field's Rindu layer, which has reserves estimated at two billion barrels.
"We are studying the development of the Rindu layer in the Duri field through injection," he said. The result of the study was expected in 1999, he said.
"We hope Rindu will offset the decline of Duri," he said.
He said Caltex would continue to explore for oil, operating in its 31,000 sq km area in Central Sumatra. Indonesia currently produces about 1.60 million bpd of crude and condensate.
Major foreign oil companies working as Pertamina contractors in Indonesia include affiliates or subsidiaries of Mobil Corp, British Petroleum and ARCO.
